section.heading: Determine Whether a Fraction is a Solution of an Equation
section.paragraph: As we saw in Solve Equations with the Subtraction and Addition Properties of Equality and Solve Equations Using Integers; The Division Property of Equality, a solution of an equation is a value that makes a true statement when substituted for the variable in the equation. In those sections, we found whole number and integer solutions to equations. Now that we have worked with fractions, we are ready to find fraction solutions to equations.
The steps we take to determine whether a number is a solution to an equation are the same whether the solution is a whole number, an integer, or a fraction.

note.title: How To
note.heading: Determine whether a number is a solution to an equation.

list.item: Step 1. Substitute the number for the variable in the equation.
Step 2. Simplify the expressions on both sides of the equation.
Step 3. Determine whether the resulting equation is true. If it is true, the number is a solution. If it is not true, the number is not a solution.

problem.paragraph: Determine whether each of the following is a solution of $$x - \frac{3}{10} = \frac{1}{2}.$$

row.cell: Change to fractions with a LCD of 10.

solution.paragraph: Since $$x = 1$$ does not result in a true equation, $$1$$ is not a solution to the equation.
Since $$x = \frac{4}{5}$$ results in a true equation, $$\frac{4}{5}$$ is a solution to the equation $$x - \frac{3}{10} = \frac{1}{2}.$$
Since $$x = - \frac{4}{5}$$ does not result in a true equation, $$- \frac{4}{5}$$ is not a solution to the equation.

section.heading: Solve Equations with Fractions Using the Multiplication Property of Equality
section.paragraph: Consider the equation $$4$$ We want to know what number divided by $$3.$$ gives $$4.$$ So to “undo” the division, we will need to multiply by $$a,b,$$ The Multiplication Property of Equality will allow us to do this. This property says that if we start with two equal quantities and multiply both by the same number, the results are equal.

note.title: The Multiplication Property of Equality
